findings.headline: Investment balances increased to £905.3m following receipt of £417m Integrated Settlement grant, managed with priority to security and liquidity
findings.detail: Following receipt of the full-year Integrated Settlement grant of £417m in April, investment balances increased significantly from £451.0m at year start to £905.3m at 30 June. The portfolio is well-diversified across deposit-taking institutions, local authorities, DMO and money market funds, with 79.4% held in 0-12 month terms for liquidity and only 1.7% beyond 12 months. Investment strategy prioritises security and liquidity before yield, in line with statutory guidance and approved treasury management strategy.
findings.matters: Large cash balances can create treasury management complexity and concentration risk; a lender wants to see that a council is managing significant liquidity prudently and not taking excessive risks to generate yield. This demonstrates disciplined investment approach.
findings.figures: Investment balances £905.3m at 30 June vs £451.0m at 1 April; increase of £454.3m mainly from Integrated Settlement grant receipt of £417m; portfolio: Banks £603.3m, Local Authorities £80.0m, DMO £85.0m, Money Market Funds £137.0m; 44.5% invested 9-12 months, 18.3% in 0-3 months
findings.quote: Investment balances increased from £451.0m at the start of the year to £905.3m at 30 June 2026, largely due to the receipt in April of the full year's Integrated Settlement grant funding of £417m. These balances are held across short-term deposits, on-call accounts, money market funds, the Debt Management Office and other local authorities, with investment decisions continuing to prioritise security and liquidity before yield.

findings.headline: External borrowing stable at £113.3m with 95.29% of portfolio at 10+ year maturity, locking in interest rate of 4.14%
findings.detail: No new borrowing was undertaken during Q1 and no early repayments made, leaving external borrowing unchanged at £113.3m (comprising £78.3m PWLB and £35.0m private sector borrowing) at an average rate of 4.14%. The maturity structure shows 95.29% of borrowing falls due in 10+ years, with minimal near-term refinancing risk. This long-dated profile locks in current interest costs and significantly reduces exposure to future rate movements.
findings.matters: Refinancing risk and debt maturity profile are key indicators of financial stability for a lender. A council with debt locked in at long maturity faces lower medium-term refinancing costs and interest rate risk.
findings.figures: External borrowing £113.3m at 4.14% average rate; PWLB £78.3m, private sector £35.0m; maturity: 95.29% due 10+ years, 4.41% due 2-5 years, 0.29% due under 12 months
findings.quote: At 30 June 2026, the Authority held £113.3 million of external loans, no change from the beginning of the year.

findings.headline: Additional staffing approved in-year driving £0.1m corporate overheads overspend, with full-year cost impact falling into 2027/28
findings.detail: Corporate overheads forecast shows expenditure of £41.3m against approved budget of £41.2m—a £0.1m overspend before recharges, driven by additional posts approved since budget was set. The original budget did not assume full-year cost of all posts in the establishment, only part-year impact of recruitment. The report notes that full-year impact of posts approved during the year will fall into 2027/28 and must be considered in MTFP refresh and future budget-setting.
findings.matters: Recurring cost increases directly affect a council's operating margin and future debt servicing capacity. Forward visibility of staffing cost trends is critical for multi-year financial planning and debt sustainability.
findings.figures: Corporate overheads £0.1m overspend (£41.3m forecast vs £41.2m budget); employee costs £23.267m forecast vs £23.165m budget (£0.102m increase); staffing-related pressure to continue into 2027/28
findings.quote: The quarter 1 forecast therefore reflects the expected part-year impact of recruitment taking place during the year, including additional posts approved since the budget was set. While this results in a relatively limited in-year pressure, the full-year impact of these posts will fall into 2027/28 and will need to be considered as part of the MTFP refresh.

findings.headline: Housing and Strategic Planning expenditure £9.8m below budget due to delays in project approvals and contracting
findings.detail: Housing programme is underspending by £9.8m, with expenditure forecast at £25.3m against budget of £35.1m. The primary driver is the Integrated Settlement housing allocation at £5.0m versus £21.9m budget. The report attributes this to the time required for projects to progress through development, appraisal, approval and contracting stages. However, the Brownfield Housing Fund continues performing, with 34 schemes approved and five complete.
findings.matters: Capital programme timing can indicate delivery capability constraints; persistent slippage in major housing initiatives affects a council's ability to execute its growth agenda and generate economic returns that support debt servicing capacity.
findings.figures: Housing expenditure £25.3m forecast vs £35.1m budget (£9.8m shortfall); Integrated Settlement housing £5.0m forecast vs £21.9m budget; Brownfield Housing Fund 34 schemes approved, 5 complete
findings.quote: Housing and Strategic Planning expenditure is forecast at £25.3m against a budget of £35.1m, representing a net variance of £9.8m below budget. The most significant movement relates to the Integrated Settlement housing allocation, where expenditure is forecast at £5.0m compared with an original budget of £21.9m.

findings.headline: Interest income forecast at £28.9m compared with approved budget of £6.8m, driven by higher cash balances and interest rates
findings.detail: Corporate overheads show net variance of £21.7m below budget, primarily due to interest income forecast at £28.9m against £6.8m budget—a £22.1m increase. This reflects higher than anticipated cash balances held during the year and current interest rates. The report explicitly states this additional interest income will be transferred to an earmarked reserve at year end and will not support recurring revenue expenditure, demonstrating prudent financial management.
findings.matters: A lender needs to understand whether a council is using investment income to mask underlying budget pressures or fund recurring costs. This council is generating significant investment income but reserving it rather than relying on it for operations.
findings.figures: Interest income £28.9m forecast vs £6.8m budget; variance of £22.1m; to be transferred to earmarked interest reserve at year end
findings.quote: The overall net corporate overheads position is forecast to be £21.7m below budget, primarily due to interest income now being forecast at £28.9m compared with the approved budget of £6.8m.

findings.paper_title: 2025 26 Outturn and 2026 27 Budget Reporting Update report
findings.headline: External borrowing reduced by £10.666m following LOBO call and repayment; debt fell from £124m to £113.333m with no new borrowing in 2025/26
findings.detail: The MSA's external borrowing decreased by £10.666m during 2025/26 from £124m to £113.333m 'due to the repayment of a Lenders Option Borrowers Option (LOBO) loan which was called in, and regular principal repayments on equal instalment of principal (EIP) loans.' Private Sector borrowing fell from £45m to £35m while PWLB borrowing remained stable at £79m to £78.333m. The paper confirms no new external borrowing was undertaken. All debt relates to inherited Transport activity, principally the second Tyne Tunnel construction and Tyne and Wear Passenger Transport Executive operations.
findings.matters: LOBO calls are refinancing events requiring cash to repay at par and funding replacement; in the current rate environment, par repayment is typically cheaper than accepting a new higher rate. Debt reduction improves the borrower's financial position and leverage ratios. For lenders, repayment execution is a positive credit signal.
findings.figures: External debt £113.333m (31 March 2026) vs £124m (1 April 2025); decrease £10.666m; LOBO repayment principal; Private Sector borrowing £35m vs £45m; PWLB £78.333m vs £79m
findings.quote: As at 31 March 2026, the MSA held £113.333 million in external borrowing, a decrease of £10.666 million from the start of the year due to the repayment of a Lenders Option Borrowers Option (LOBO) loan which was called in, and regular principal repayments on equal instalment of principal (EIP) loans.

findings.paper_title: 2025 26 Outturn and 2026 27 Budget Reporting Update report
findings.headline: Capital programmes delivered £524.7m against revised budget £532.5m, with £54.6m below Q3 forecast driven by delays on Investment Zones, BSIP Capital and Brownfield Housing Fund
findings.detail: Service delivery programme expenditure (revenue and capital) totalled £524.7m against a revised budget of £532.5m, representing an underspend of £7.7m. However, outturn was £54.6m below the Q3 forecast of £309.1m, indicating material slippage from forecast. Major capital schemes significantly underdelivered: Investment Zones £5.8m actual vs £13.3m forecast; BSIP Capital £7.5m vs £16m forecast; Brownfield Housing Fund £14m vs £19m forecast; Other capital schemes £9.7m below budget. The paper attributes these variances to delays from 'programme pressures, rescoping, or local decision making' which 'deferred spend into future years'. On Investment Zones specifically, projects are now in delivery but 'have only recently begun to submit claims; spend to date therefore remains low against profile despite significant committed funding' with 'material increase in expenditure anticipated in 2026/27'.
findings.matters: Capital slippage affects medium-term borrowing forecasts and treasury planning; large variances between forecast and outturn signal delivery risks that peers and lenders factor into financial assessments and covenant monitoring. The £54.6m variance represents 18% of the Q3 forecast and is material for creditor exposure.
findings.figures: Capital programmes £524.7m actual vs £532.5m revised budget (underspend £7.7m); Q3 forecast £309.1m (adverse variance £54.6m or 18%); Investment Zones £5.8m vs £13.3m forecast; BSIP Capital £7.5m vs £16m; Brownfield Housing £14m vs £19m; Other capital £22.7m vs £32.4m budget
findings.quote: A number of schemes experienced delivery delays due to programme pressures, rescoping, or local decision making, which has deferred spend into future years and resulted in slippage against the previous forecast.

findings.paper_title: 2025 26 Outturn and 2026 27 Budget Reporting Update report
findings.headline: Interest income £22.445m exceeded revised budget by £15.645m reflecting strong investment returns and higher cash balances; £19.4m transferred to new Interest Reserve
findings.detail: The MSA achieved a provisional outturn surplus of £20.339m against a revised budget surplus of £1.370m, a favourable variance of £18.969m. Income was £17.108m higher than budget, driven principally by interest income of £22.445m against a revised budget of £6.800m. This was £0.970m higher than Q3 forecast. Rather than embedding this windfall into ongoing revenue budget, the MSA proposes to transfer £19.4m to a newly-created Interest Reserve to provide flexible funding for priority projects through the Single Assurance Framework, with a further £1m to the Pension Reserve to support employer pension contributions from the 2025 triennial valuation.
findings.matters: Finance directors track how peers manage temporary income gains during periods of elevated interest rates; the practice of reserving one-off gains rather than building them into baseline budgets signals financial discipline. For lenders, the MSA's £451m investment position against £113m borrowing demonstrates strong liquidity and financial stability.
findings.figures: Interest income £22.445m actual vs £6.800m revised budget (variance £15.645m); total surplus £20.339m actual vs £1.370m revised budget; £19.4m to Interest Reserve; £1m to Pension Reserve; total investments £451.014m at 31 March 2026
findings.quote: interest income of £22.445m, which is £15.645m above the revised budget and £0.970m higher than the Q3 forecast, reflecting continued strong investment returns and higher than forecast cash balances during the year. As previously set out to Cabinet, in line with the Medium Term Financial Plan, it is proposed that the surplus is transferred to a new earmarked interest reserve, to provide a flexible funding source for priority projects brought forward through the Single Assurance Framework.

findings.paper_title: 9 Internal Audit Annual Report and Opinion 2025-26
findings.headline: Internal Audit external quality assessment overdue by three years, last completed in February 2018
findings.detail: Global Internal Audit Standards in the UK Public Sector require external quality assessments of internal audit functions every five years. North Tyneside's internal audit function was last subject to external assessment in February 2018, making it overdue since February 2023. The Chief Internal Auditor notes there are no specific sanctions arising from this non-conformance and considers the risk to be low given annual self-assessments against standards. The authority plans to commence an exercise to consider arrangements for completion of an external assessment in 2026/27.
findings.matters: External quality assessments are a key governance mechanism for assuring the independence, objectivity and effectiveness of the internal audit function itself; an overdue assessment represents a governance oversight material to audit committees and those monitoring audit governance.
findings.figures: Assessment required every five years; last completed February 2018; currently overdue since February 2023
findings.quote: This is required every five years, but North Tyneside's Internal Audit service was last subject to external assessment in February 2018.

findings.paper_title: 9 Internal Audit Annual Report and Opinion 2025-26
findings.headline: Chief Internal Auditor provides Reasonable Assurance that governance, risk management and control frameworks are adequately designed and operating effectively
findings.detail: The internal audit annual opinion concludes that the North East MSA's governance, risk management and control frameworks are adequately designed and operating effectively to support achievement of objectives. This is stated as a positive opinion reflecting a generally sound system of governance, risk management and internal control. The opinion is based on assurance reviews conducted during 2025/26 of key operational areas including the Single Assurance Framework, Health and Safety, Information Governance, and other core business functions.
findings.matters: The annual internal audit opinion on governance, risk management and control framework effectiveness is a key input to the Annual Governance Statement and provides assurance to external stakeholders including lenders on the council's control environment and risk management maturity.
findings.figures: No numerical figures; opinion is a qualitative assessment expressed as Reasonable Assurance
findings.quote: Based upon the work undertaken by Internal Audit and all information known at the time of preparing this report, the Chief Internal Auditor provides Reasonable Assurance that the North East MSA's governance, risk management and control frameworks are adequately designed and operating effectively to support achievement of objectives.

findings.headline: Authority expanded payroll from 193 to 292 staff in two years and created in-house governance functions to reduce reliance on council service-level agreements.
findings.detail: Headcount grew from 193 employees in May 2024 to 292 in May 2026. New roles established include heads of Policy, Planning and Performance; Technology and Transformation; Data and Analysis; in-house lawyers; and a Senior Risk Manager. The shift from reliance on service-level agreements with other councils for risk, legal, and procurement support to in-house capability will have ongoing cost implications.
findings.matters: Major staffing expansion signals operating cost structure change. A peer council or lender needs to understand whether the growth reflects permanent run rate or reflects temporary setup of a new authority, and the sustainability of that staffing level.
findings.figures: Headcount: 193 (May 2024) to 292 (May 2026)
findings.quote: The total number of employees grew from 193 in May 2024 to 292 in May 2026.

findings.headline: Audit and Standards Committee and Overview and Scrutiny Committee experienced quoracy failures during 2025/26.
findings.detail: Both governance oversight committees were unable to convene on some occasions due to lack of member attendance. The authority addressed this by introducing payment of allowances to committee members, approved by Cabinet on 9 June 2026, following a recommendation from the Independent Renumeration Panel. The ASC Chair highlighted the quoracy risk in his presentation to Cabinet.
findings.matters: Quoracy failures prevent committees from delivering independent oversight of finance, audit, and risk; they represent a governance control gap. This signals the authority faced engagement or capacity challenges in its first year of operation.
findings.figures: Quoracy issues in both ASC and OSC during 2025/26; remedied June 2026
findings.quote: Both Audit and Standards and Overview and Scrutiny committees encountered quoracy issues in 2025/26. To reduce the risk of this happening in future, a series of steps have been taken: the payment of allowances to committee members, as recommended by the Independent Renumeration Panel, was agreed by Cabinet at its meeting on 9 June 2026.

findings.headline: Unqualified audit opinion on first set of accounts completed ahead of deadline, with no reported value-for-money weaknesses.
findings.detail: The North East MSA's external auditors completed the audit of the statement of accounts for the year ending 31 March 2025 ahead of the statutory backstop date of 27 February 2026. The audit produced an unqualified opinion without modification. The auditors concluded there were no significant weaknesses in arrangements for securing economy, efficiency and effectiveness in use of resources.
findings.matters: For a newly established authority, a clean audit opinion on first accounts signals adequate governance framework and financial management systems; lenders assess the control environment partly through audit opinions.
findings.figures: Unqualified opinion; no significant weaknesses reported; deadline met
findings.quote: The external auditors issued an unqualified opinion, without modification, on the financial statements, in advance of the statutory backstop date of 27 February 2026.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Auditor's Draft Annual Report 2024-25
findings.headline: Audit work commenced November 2025 with expected completion February 2026 for year ended 31 March 2025
findings.detail: Audit work on 2024-25 financial statements commenced in November 2025 with completion expected February 2026. This draft report issued 28 November 2025. Creates 11-month lag between financial year-end and expected audit completion, reflecting complexity of first-year consolidation audit combining two merged authorities.
findings.matters: Extended audit timeline delays finalization of financial statements; indicates complexity in consolidating accounts and operations from two predecessor authorities.
findings.figures: Year ended 31 March 2025, audit work commenced November 2025, completion expected February 2026
findings.quote: Work has just started in November 2025 on the accounts audit, and we expect to complete in February 2026.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Auditor's Draft Annual Report 2024-25
findings.headline: Authority's Performance Management Framework remains in development; Cabinet approval planned December 2025, outcomes framework by 31 March 2026
findings.detail: Key performance management framework not yet approved at end of first full financial year of newly formed authority. Outcomes framework for Integrated Settlement also in development with March 2026 finalization target. Foundational performance systems still being established.
findings.matters: Foundational performance frameworks not yet finalized 11 months into operation indicates organization in establishment phase; relevant to assessing maturity of performance monitoring during consolidation.
findings.figures: Cabinet approval December 2025, outcomes framework finalization by 31 March 2026
findings.quote: The Authority's Performance Management Framework is currently in development and will be presented to the North East CA Cabinet for approval in December 2025.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Auditor's Draft Annual Report 2024-25
findings.headline: Auditor identified no significant weaknesses in value for money arrangements across financial sustainability, governance, and service delivery efficiency
findings.detail: Auditor found no risks of significant weaknesses and no actual significant weaknesses across all three VFM criteria. Clean assessment delivered despite Authority being only 11 months old at year-end, having been formed from consolidation of two authorities and operating under newly established governance model.
findings.matters: Clean audit opinion on governance and arrangements after major structural reorganization indicates new governance model stood up effectively despite complexity of first year.
findings.figures: None
findings.quote: We did not identify any significant weaknesses in the Authority's arrangements to secure economy, efficiency and effectiveness in its use of resources.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Auditor's Draft Annual Report 2024-25
findings.headline: Authority held £482.1 million in useable reserves as at 31 March 2025
findings.detail: Strong reserves position at end of first financial year of newly formed combined authority. Reserves include those inherited from predecessor authorities plus any surplus from 2024-25 operations, providing financial buffer for organizational integration and emerging service pressures.
findings.matters: Large reserves indicate financial resilience in newly formed organization navigating consolidation and establishing new governance model.
findings.figures: £482.1 million useable reserves
findings.quote: As at 31 March 2025, the Authority reported useable reserves of £482.1 million in the draft accounts.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Auditor's Draft Annual Report 2024-25
findings.headline: North East Combined Authority established 7 May 2024 from merger of two predecessor authorities under new mayoral governance structure
findings.detail: Major regional governance reorganization in which North of Tyne Combined Authority and previous North East Combined Authority formally ceased 6 May 2024. New North East Mayoral Combined Authority established with directly elected mayor (elected 2 May 2024), consolidating seven constituent councils—County Durham, Gateshead, Newcastle, North Tyneside, Northumberland, South Tyneside and Sunderland—under unified mayoral framework. Material change in regional governance model.
findings.matters: Structural reorganization affects governance model and organizational complexity; lenders and peers need to assess execution in first year of new mayoral model.
findings.figures: Seven constituent councils, established 7 May 2024
findings.quote: Following a major reorganisation of regional governance across the North East of England, both the North of Tyne Combined Authority (NTCA) and the North East Combined Authority (NECA), in its previous form, formally ceased to exist on 6 May 2024.

findings.headline: Related party declaration forms not obtained from all officers and members; online system being introduced
findings.detail: Audit identified a control deficiency (non-significant) where not all related party declaration forms were obtained from senior officers and members during the audit year. Management is responding by introducing online declaration forms with automatic reminders from April 2025 to strengthen this control.
findings.matters: Related party declarations are a key governance control for identifying conflicts of interest. Though classified as non-significant, the issue highlights post-merger process gaps and the prompt remedial action demonstrates management responsiveness.
findings.figures: Specific numbers of incomplete forms not disclosed
findings.quote: As part of the related parties review, it was identified that not all related party declaration forms had been obtained for the period under audit. Although forms are issued annually, some forms had not been completed and returned.

findings.headline: External investments figure understated by £60m in initial opening balance statement; corrected following audit
findings.detail: Audit of opening balances transferred from the two predecessor authorities identified material errors in the Narrative Report. Short-term external investments were stated as £400.119m when the correct balance is £460.024m. The figure for total external borrowing transferred in was also incorrectly stated for the long-term element only rather than total borrowing. All corrections were accepted by management before publication.
findings.matters: The £60m variance in reported external investment position is material. Indicates merger data migration issues were present but identified and resolved through audit; lenders care about accuracy of asset positions, peer finance directors care about merger accounting quality.
findings.figures: £400.119m incorrectly stated; £460.024m correct balance; variance of approximately £60m
findings.quote: the short-term external investments figure transferred across was incorrectly stated as £400.119m. This has been corrected to show the correct balance of £460.024m.

findings.headline: Value for money audit identifies no significant weaknesses
findings.detail: Work on the Authority's arrangements to secure economy, efficiency and effectiveness in its use of resources under the 2024 Code of Audit Practice has been completed with no significant weaknesses identified requiring recommendations.
findings.matters: VFM audit findings can reveal underlying financial sustainability or strategic efficiency problems. Their absence is material to understanding the organisation's financial health and management effectiveness.
findings.figures: No significant weaknesses identified
findings.quote: We anticipate having no significant weaknesses in arrangements to report in relation to the arrangements that the Authority has in place to secure economy, efficiency and effectiveness in its use of resources.

findings.headline: First-year audit of merged combined authority receives unqualified opinion
findings.detail: The auditor anticipates issuing an unqualified opinion without modification on the new Authority's first set of accounts, covering the year ended 31 March 2025. This was a complex first audit requiring lower performance materiality, higher sample sizes and detailed technical review due to the new entity created from merger of two predecessor authorities.
findings.matters: A clean audit opinion on a newly merged entity is essential for lender confidence and market trust in the combined authority's financial reporting and integration.
findings.figures: Final Group materiality £12.161m; North East Combined Authority £9.044m; performance materiality Group £8.513m, Authority £6.331m
findings.quote: At the time of issuing this report and subject to the satisfactory conclusion of our remaining audit work, we anticipate issuing an unqualified opinion, without modification, as set out in Appendix C.
